parts.gloss: is fit to be / will be

literal: The enmity of him who has blind anger and him who has excessively great lust is fit to be desired.
translation: The hostility of one who has blind, unreasoning anger and excessive, uncontrolled lust is a state to be welcomed and desired by his adversaries.
modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காத குருட்டுத்தனமான கோபத்தை உடையவன், அளவற்ற பேராசை உடையவன் ஆகியோரது பகையானது (அவர்களை எளிதில் வெல்லலாம் என்பதால்) விரும்பத்தக்கதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains whose enmity is advantageous to seek or welcome. A person who is blinded by anger ('காணாச் சினத்தான்') cannot think rationally or assess situations. Similarly, one driven by excessive lust or desire ('கழிபெருங் காமத்தான்') is easily distracted and weakened by his passions. Their hostility ('பேணாமை') is to be welcomed ('பேணப் படும்') because their inherent flaws make them easy to defeat, turning their enmity into an opportunity for their rivals.
